q: Which channel sizes break out most, and are their audiences happy? Give n.
a:
Small channels break out most: 31 of 83 videos (37.3%) were outperformers, versus 10 of 49 mid-size (20.4%) and 2 of 38 large (5.3%). Small channels' average relative lift was 7.8x, mid 3.5x, large 1.2x.

Audience mood is mildly positive overall, but it doesn't track breakout rate. Mid-size channels are happiest: net sentiment +0.13 (43.6% positive, 30.4% negative, n=2,134 product comments). Small channels are +0.07 (39.9% positive, 32.8% negative, n=2,470). Large channels are roughly neutral at -0.01 (37.4% positive, 38.1% negative, n=1,839).

Caveat: the large group has only 2 outperformers, so its rate is shaky. These are associations from a comment sample, not proof that channel size drives either result.
sql: WITH base AS (SELECT c.video_id, CASE WHEN cr.tier IN ('nano <50k','micro 50-250k') THEN 'small' WHEN cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' THEN 'mid' WHEN cr.tier IN ('macro 1-5M','mega 5M+') THEN 'large' END AS size_group, p.outperformer, p.rel_lift FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official'), lift AS (SELECT size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, SUM(outperformer) AS n_outperformers, ROUND(AVG(outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(rel_lift),3) AS mean_rel_lift FROM base WHERE outperformer IS NOT NULL GROUP BY size_group), sent AS (SELECT b.size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_product_comments, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_sent FROM comments m JOIN base b ON b.video_id=m.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY b.size_group) SELECT l.size_group, l.n_videos, l.n_outperformers, l.outperformer_rate, l.mean_rel_lift, s.n_product_comments, s.pct_positive, s.pct_negative, CASE WHEN s.n_product_comments>=10 THEN s.net_sent END AS net_sentiment FROM lift l LEFT JOIN sent s ON s.size_group=l.size_group ORDER BY l.outperformer_rate DESC LIMIT 10

q: Which content formats work best for mid-sized channels?
a:
First impressions is the only format with a meaningful sample (n=19) and decent results: 36.8% outperformed, with a median rel_lift of 1.965 (mean 2.523).

Full review (n=1, rate 100%, lift 15.4) and durability test (n=1, 100%, lift 6.4) look best on paper, but a single video each is an anecdote, not a pattern.

Explainer tips (n=7) shows a mean lift of 10.2 but a median of 0.486 and only 14.3% outperforming, so one or two big hits are skewing it.

Comparison (n=6) and upgrade advice (n=8) had no outperformers, with median lifts of 1.318 and 0.729. Meme shorts (n=4, one lacking a baseline), keynote recaps (n=2) and other (n=2) also had none, but those samples are too small to judge.

Caveat: these are associations in small samples, not proof that format drives performance.
sql: WITH b AS (SELECT c.video_id, c.format, p.rel_lift, p.outperformer FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND cr.tier='mid 250k-1M'), r AS (SELECT format, rel_lift, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY format ORDER BY rel_lift) rn, count(*) OVER (PARTITION BY format) cnt FROM b WHERE rel_lift IS NOT NULL), med AS (SELECT format, avg(rel_lift) AS median_rel_lift FROM r WHERE rn IN ((cnt+1)/2,(cnt+2)/2) GROUP BY format) SELECT b.format, count(*) AS n_videos, count(b.outperformer) AS n_with_baseline, round(avg(b.outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, round(avg(b.rel_lift),3) AS mean_rel_lift, round(m.median_rel_lift,3) AS median_rel_lift FROM b LEFT JOIN med m ON m.format=b.format GROUP BY b.format ORDER BY outperformer_rate DESC, median_rel_lift DESC LIMIT 40

q: Which high-lift videos have the most negative audience reaction? Name two examples, with lift and sentiment shown separately.
a:
The two most negative high-lift videos are "iPhone Duo's Camera Disappears #shorts" (Time Travel Visuals) and "iPhone FOLD Hands-On | Apple COOKED!" (TechDroider).

- Camera Disappears: lift 498.37 (rel_lift 67.7) on about 20.4M views. Net sentiment is -0.585 (n=65 product-side comments), with 69% negative and 11% positive.
- FOLD Hands-On: lift 86.76 (rel_lift 11.8) on about 2.0M views. Net sentiment is -0.571 (n=49), with 71% negative and 14% positive.

Lift and sentiment are separate measures here. Both videos got outsized attention and a mostly negative product-side reaction.

Caveat: these are associations from sampled comments, not proof that the videos caused the reaction. The n values are modest, so treat the percentages as rough.
sql: WITH s AS (SELECT video_id, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, SUM(sentiment='positive') AS pos, SUM(sentiment='negative') AS neg FROM comments WHERE lang='en' AND trivial=0 AND target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY video_id) SELECT c.video_id, c.title, cr.name AS channel_name, c.format, p.views, ROUND(p.lift,3) AS lift, ROUND(p.rel_lift,3) AS rel_lift, s.n_product_side, ROUND(s.pos*1.0/s.n_product_side,3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(s.neg*1.0/s.n_product_side,3) AS pct_negative, ROUND((s.pos-s.neg)*1.0/s.n_product_side,3) AS net_sentiment FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id JOIN s ON s.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND p.outperformer=1 AND s.n_product_side>=10 ORDER BY net_sentiment ASC, p.rel_lift DESC LIMIT 5

q: Which audience topics are largest, and which are growing fastest this week?
a:
Samsung Did It First is the largest topic: 683 comments, 7.4% of the 9,184 in scope. Next are Praise for review quality (504, 5.5%), Apple ad parody humor (435, 4.7%), Eager to Buy (428, 4.7%) and Folding Phone Durability Doubts (407, 4.4%).

By raw gain this week vs. the prior week, Samsung Did It First leads (70 to 169, +99), then Eager to Buy (53 to 147, +94), Left-Handed Concerns (+68) and Apple ad parody humor (+62).

By growth rate, Left-Handed Concerns is highest at 5.5x (15 to 83). Waiting for Next Year is 5.2x (9 to 47), Apple Software Integration 4.3x (7 to 30) and Wanting Pro Cameras 3.8x (9 to 34).

Caveat: the fast risers start from small prior-week counts (n of 7 to 15), so the ratios exaggerate. Nearly every topic rose, so part of this is overall volume growth. Only Love for creator's videos fell (14 to 11).
sql: WITH sc AS (SELECT cm.topic_id, cm.day_since_launch AS d FROM comments cm JOIN content ct ON ct.video_id=cm.video_id WHERE ct.topic='duo' AND ct.format!='official' AND cm.lang='en' AND cm.trivial=0), mx AS (SELECT MAX(d) AS m FROM sc), tot AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS t FROM sc), agg AS (SELECT topic_id, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(CASE WHEN d > m-7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS wk, SUM(CASE WHEN d <= m-7 AND d > m-14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS prev FROM sc, mx WHERE topic_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY topic_id) SELECT t.topic_id, t.name, t.pool, t.origin, t.first_seen, a.n AS n_total, tot.t AS n_scope_comments, ROUND(1.0*a.n/tot.t,3) AS share_of_comments, a.wk AS n_this_week, a.prev AS n_prior_week, a.wk - a.prev AS change, ROUND(1.0*a.wk/NULLIF(a.prev,0),3) AS wow_ratio, mx.m AS latest_day FROM agg a JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=a.topic_id, tot, mx ORDER BY a.n DESC LIMIT 40

q: How does audience sentiment on the iPhone Duo compare with the iPhone 18 Pro?
a:
Sentiment is a bit better for the iPhone 18 Pro than the Duo, mostly because it draws fewer negative comments. Overall net sentiment is +0.145 for the 18 Pro (n=3,087) versus +0.069 for the Duo (n=6,443). Positive shares are almost identical (40.3% vs 40.4%), but negative is 25.7% for the 18 Pro vs 33.5% for the Duo.

By target:
- Product: 18 Pro +0.216 (n=2,552), Duo +0.158 (n=4,517).
- Price/value: both negative, Duo -0.555 (n=672), 18 Pro -0.432 (n=229).
- Competitor: both positive, 18 Pro +0.412 (n=187), Duo +0.346 (n=755).
- Apple brand: Duo -0.313 (n=499), but 18 Pro is much worse at -0.672 (n=119).

Caveat: this is a sample of comments, and the 18 Pro brand and competitor groups have small n, so those gaps are less firm.
sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT c.topic AS topic, m.target AS target, m.sentiment AS sentiment
  FROM comments m
  JOIN content c ON c.video_id = m.video_id
  WHERE c.topic IN ('duo','iphone_18_pro')
    AND c.format != 'official'
    AND m.lang = 'en' AND m.trivial = 0
    AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor')
),
rolled AS (
  SELECT topic, 'all product-side' AS target, sentiment FROM base
  UNION ALL
  SELECT topic, target, sentiment FROM base
)
SELECT topic, target,
  COUNT(*) AS n_product_side,
  ROUND(AVG(sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive,
  ROUND(AVG(sentiment='neutral'),3) AS pct_neutral,
  ROUND(AVG(sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative,
  ROUND(AVG(sentiment='positive') - AVG(sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_sentiment,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(*) >= 10 THEN 'ok' ELSE 'n<10, not judged' END AS reliability
FROM rolled
GROUP BY topic, target
ORDER BY target != 'all product-side', target, topic
LIMIT 40

q: What do people like most about the Duo, and what do they criticise most?
a:
Most-liked: excitement to buy. "Eager to Buy" (n=428) has a 47% positive share against 22% negative, with some people planning upgrades from Pro Max or Z Fold phones. Cases and accessories (n=230, 46% positive) and the near-invisible crease and fold animation (n=254, 46.5% positive) also lean positive.

Most-criticised: the clearest negative lean is the under-display camera (n=275, 40% negative vs 25% positive). Price (n=385, 39.7% negative), durability doubts (n=407, 39.1%) and "Samsung did it first" (n=683, 37.8%) are also criticised, but each is split almost evenly between positive and negative.

Caveat: these are topic-level tags on a comment sample, and most topics mix both sentiments. They show association, not cause, and "liked" topics still carry plenty of negative comments (e.g., Samsung comparisons are 31% negative, n=400).
sql: WITH c AS (SELECT cm.topic_id, cm.sentiment FROM comments cm JOIN content ct ON ct.video_id=cm.video_id WHERE ct.topic='duo' AND ct.format!='official' AND cm.lang='en' AND cm.trivial=0 AND cm.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor')), t AS (SELECT tp.topic_id, tp.name, tp.summary, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(c.sentiment='positive') AS n_pos, SUM(c.sentiment='negative') AS n_neg, ROUND(1.0*SUM(c.sentiment='positive')/COUNT(*),3) AS pos_share, ROUND(1.0*SUM(c.sentiment='negative')/COUNT(*),3) AS neg_share FROM c JOIN topics tp ON tp.topic_id=c.topic_id WHERE tp.pool='product' GROUP BY tp.topic_id, tp.name, tp.summary HAVING COUNT(*)>=10), liked AS (SELECT 'liked' AS side, name, summary, n, n_pos, n_neg, pos_share, neg_share FROM t WHERE n_pos>0 ORDER BY n_pos DESC LIMIT 8), crit AS (SELECT 'criticised' AS side, name, summary, n, n_pos, n_neg, pos_share, neg_share FROM t WHERE n_neg>0 ORDER BY n_neg DESC LIMIT 8) SELECT * FROM liked UNION ALL SELECT * FROM crit LIMIT 40
